summary: I directly inspected `/app/jump_analyzer.py` (it defines `detect_jump_frames(video_path)` using OpenCV/Numpy and the recorded run shows it was invoked on `/app/example_video.mp4` and wrote `/app/output.toml`), `/app/output.toml` (it contains exactly `jump_takeoff_frame_number = 72` and `jump_land_frame_number = 90` with scalar integer values and no extra fields), and `/app/jump_probe.jpg` via a read-only artifact perception (frames around 72 show the athlete leaving the scene, while by 73 onward the athlete is absent, consistent with takeoff preceding landing). The reported frames are in range and ordered correctly.
